en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province is famous for having the most perfect cone shape of any volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle, the national bird, is critically endangered and easily recognized by its distinctive crest of long, dark brown feathers.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the West Philippine Sea.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching a peak elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater lake that uniquely contains Volcano Island, which itself features a smaller main crater lake.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting hundreds of marine species.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over one thousand symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry summer season.
The Philippines is a top global producer of nickel, a valuable metal primarily mined from laterite deposits in Surigao and Palawan.
The amihan is the cool northeast monsoon that brings dry, pleasant weather to the Philippines between November and February.
The waling-waling, scientifically named Vanda sanderiana, is a rare and highly prized orchid species native to the montane forests of Mindanao.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches over five hundred kilometers along eastern Luzon, acting as a natural barrier against Pacific typhoons.
The Philippine Trench is a major oceanic depression east of the archipelago, reaching its maximum depth at a point called the Emden Deep.
